cv-5b516d51.stem: Which statement about the left ventricle is false?
options: It has two papillary muscles, anterior and posterior.
It forms the apex of the heart.
The mitral valve has two cusps.
Its wall is about three times thicker than that of the right ventricle.
Its outflow tract contains the conus arteriosus (infundibulum).
cv-5b516d51.explanation: The conus arteriosus (infundibulum) is the smooth-walled outflow tract of the right ventricle. The outflow tract of the left ventricle is called the aortic vestibule. Because the left ventricle works against systemic pressure, its wall is the thickest of all the chambers.

cv-258cd59d.stem: Which option lists the branches of the aortic arch correctly from right to left?
options: Brachiocephalic trunk, left subclavian artery, left common carotid artery
Left common carotid artery, brachiocephalic trunk, left subclavian artery
Brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid artery, left subclavian artery
Coronary arteries, brachiocephalic trunk, left subclavian artery
Right subclavian artery, right common carotid artery, left common carotid artery
cv-258cd59d.explanation: The aortic arch usually gives three branches. The brachiocephalic trunk divides behind the right sternoclavicular joint into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. The coronary arteries arise from the ascending aorta.

cv-0bdc88fc.stem: A 16-year-old hypertensive patient has high blood pressure in the arms and weak, delayed pulses in the legs. The chest X-ray shows notching of the lower borders of the ribs. Enlargement of which vessels causes the notching?
cv-0bdc88fc.explanation: In coarctation of the aorta (usually at the level of the ligamentum arteriosum) blood reaches the descending aorta via subclavian artery → internal thoracic artery → anterior intercostal arteries → posterior intercostal arteries. The enlarged posterior intercostal arteries erode the lower borders of the ribs (ribs 3–8).

cv-f7249148.stem: At which level does the abdominal aorta divide into the two common iliac arteries?
options: L4 (about the level of the umbilicus)
cv-f7249148.explanation: After the aortic hiatus (T12) the abdominal aorta descends to the left of the spine and divides at L4; this point corresponds roughly to just below the umbilicus and to the line of the iliac crests.

cv-dc7a4413.stem: A pulsatile abdominal mass is found in a 70-year-old male smoker. Where are abdominal aortic aneurysms most commonly located?
options: At the level of the origins of the renal arteries
Below the renal arteries (infrarenal), above the bifurcation
cv-dc7a4413.explanation: Most abdominal aortic aneurysms are infrarenal. In this region there are few vasa vasorum and the elastin content is low. The risk of rupture increases with diameter.

cv-7d92b3b7.stem: At which level does the common carotid artery usually divide into the internal and external carotid arteries?
options: Upper border of the thyroid cartilage (C4)
Above the angle of the mandible (C2)
cv-7d92b3b7.explanation: The carotid bifurcation lies at the level of the upper border of the thyroid cartilage. Here the dilatation at the start of the ICA (carotid sinus) is a baroreceptor and the small body at the bifurcation (carotid body) a chemoreceptor; both are supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

cv-64588484.stem: Carotid sinus massage is performed on a patient with supraventricular tachycardia. What are the afferent and efferent pathways of the fall in heart rate?
options: Afferent: vagus nerve – Efferent: glossopharyngeal nerve
Afferent: hypoglossal nerve – Efferent: vagus nerve
Afferent: glossopharyngeal nerve – Efferent: vagus nerve
Afferent: sympathetic chain – Efferent: phrenic nerve
Afferent: accessory nerve – Efferent: vagus nerve
cv-64588484.explanation: The baroreceptors of the carotid sinus report the rise in pressure to the brainstem through the carotid sinus branch of CN IX; in response vagal output increases and the heart slows. In the elderly hypersensitivity can cause syncope.

cv-b380c127.stem: Which artery gives no branches at all in the neck?
cv-b380c127.explanation: The internal carotid artery enters the carotid canal without branching in the neck; its first important branch is the ophthalmic artery inside the skull. This helps surgeons tell the ICA from the ECA.

cv-d408d339.stem: Which of the following is NOT a branch of the external carotid artery?
cv-d408d339.explanation: Branches of the ECA: superior thyroid, ascending pharyngeal, lingual, facial, occipital and posterior auricular arteries, and the terminal maxillary and superficial temporal arteries. The ophthalmic artery is the first intracranial branch of the ICA.

cv-c6279338.stem: The middle meningeal artery is a branch of which artery?
cv-c6279338.explanation: The maxillary artery gives off the middle meningeal artery in the infratemporal fossa; it enters the skull through the foramen spinosum and supplies most of the dura and the skull bones.

cv-7afbacff.stem: Where on the face is the pulse of the facial artery most easily felt?
options: Behind the angle of the mandible
At the medial angle of the eye
At the anterior border of masseter, on the lower border of the mandible
cv-7afbacff.explanation: The facial artery crosses the lower border of the mandible at the anterior border of masseter, where it can be felt against the bone. It runs a tortuous course from the corner of the mouth to the medial angle of the eye (angular artery).

cv-937ce9d9.stem: A 70-year-old woman has new temple pain, jaw pain on chewing and blurred vision; the ESR is raised. From which artery is a biopsy most often taken for diagnosis?
cv-937ce9d9.explanation: Giant cell (temporal) arteritis involves medium and large arteries, especially branches of the ECA. The superficial temporal artery, easily felt in front of the tragus, is suitable for biopsy. If treatment is delayed, involvement of the ophthalmic artery can cause permanent blindness.

cv-43492b44.stem: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) is a branch of which artery?
cv-43492b44.explanation: PICA is usually the largest intracranial branch of the vertebral artery. AICA and SCA arise from the basilar artery, which divides at the upper border of the pons into the two PCAs. Occlusion of PICA causes lateral medullary syndrome.

cv-0adf4674.stem: Which of the following arteries is NOT part of the circle of Willis (circulus arteriosus cerebri)?
cv-0adf4674.explanation: The circle of Willis is formed by the ACom, the A1 segments of both ACAs, the terminal parts of both ICAs, both PComs and the P1 segments of both PCAs. The MCA continues the ICA but is not part of the ring.

cv-11e9072b.stem: A 65-year-old patient has sudden painless complete loss of vision in one eye. On fundoscopy the retina is pale and the macula has a 'cherry-red spot'. Which artery is occluded?
cv-11e9072b.explanation: The central retinal artery is a branch of the ophthalmic artery and enters the eye within the optic nerve. Being an end artery, its occlusion makes the inner layers of the retina ischaemic; the fovea, supplied by the choroid, appears as a red spot.
